title: GCSE Statistics
summary: The whole GCSE in sixteen short chapters: the key words, the formulas and a few worked lines each, in the order of the Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Statistics specification.
subject: Statistics

title: Charts for numbers
topics: Stem & Leaf Diagrams, Frequency Polygons, Histograms

title: Averages
topics: Mean, Median, Mode, Averages from a Table, Averages from Grouped Data

title: Measures of spread
topics: Range, Box Plots & Quartiles, Cumulative Frequency

title: Probability
topics: Basic Probability, Listing Outcomes & Sample Space, Relative Frequency & Expectation, Venn Diagrams & Set Notation, Tree Diagrams, Conditional Probability

html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="Black spots on a rose leaf; it yellows and falls early, so the plant photosynthesises less; spores spread in wind and water"><g class="s1"><path d="M60,80 q100,-70 200,0 q-100,70 -200,0 z M60,80 H260" class="pt cool"/><text x="160" y="150" class="cap cool">rose leaf</text></g><g class="s2"><circle cx="120" cy="70" r="6" class="fill mv-pulse"/><circle cx="170" cy="92" r="6" class="fill mv-pulse"/><circle cx="210" cy="66" r="6" class="fill mv-pulse"/><circle cx="140" cy="95" r="6" class="fill mv-pulse"/><text x="160" y="25" class="cap">black spots</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="280" cy="60" r="2" class="fill mv-jig"/><circle cx="300" cy="45" r="2" class="fill mv-jig"/><circle cx="320" cy="70" r="2" class="fill mv-jig"/><circle cx="340" cy="50" r="2" class="fill mv-jig"/><path d="M270,80 L370,40 M364.0,39.3 L370,40 L366.2,44.6" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="330" y="95" class="cap">spores: wind, water</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="125" class="cap hot">less photosynthesis, less growth</text><text x="320" y="145" class="cap cool">fungicide, burn leaves</text></g></svg>

title: Malaria and its vector
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="A mosquito carries the malaria protist from one person to another"><g class="s1"><circle cx="60" cy="40" r="9" class="pt"/><line x1="60" y1="49" x2="60" y2="80" class="pt"/><path d="M46,62 H74 M60,80 l-10,20 M60,80 l10,20" class="pt"/><text x="60" y="135" class="cap">infected</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:200px"><ellipse cx="90" cy="30" rx="12" ry="5" class="pt"/><path d="M78,30 l-10,-2 M90,25 l-6,-10 M96,25 l6,-10" class="pt"/><text x="90" y="55" class="cap">mosquito</text></g></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="320" cy="40" r="9" class="pt"/><line x1="320" y1="49" x2="320" y2="80" class="pt"/><path d="M306,62 H334 M320,80 l-10,20 M320,80 l10,20" class="pt"/><text x="320" y="135" class="cap">bitten</text><text x="200" y="95" class="cap">vector carries the protist</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="155" class="cap cool">stop breeding, use nets</text></g></svg>

title: Phagocytosis
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="A white blood cell surrounds a pathogen, engulfs it and digests it"><g class="s1"><circle cx="110" cy="75" r="35" class="pt"/><text x="110" y="130" class="cap">white blood cell</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:-60px"><rect x="250" y="68" width="26" height="14" rx="7" class="pt hot"/></g><text x="260" y="50" class="cap hot">pathogen</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M145,55 q40,-10 50,20 q-10,30 -50,20" class="pt mv-pulse"/><text x="230" y="120" class="cap">engulfed</text></g><g class="s4"><circle cx="105" cy="70" r="2" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="115" cy="80" r="2" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="100" cy="82" r="2" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><text x="200" y="145" class="cap">digested by enzymes</text></g></svg>

title: Vaccination
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Antibody level after a vaccine and after the real pathogen: the second response is faster and much bigger"><g class="s1"><path d="M40,15 V140 H380" class="pt"/><text x="210" y="160" class="cap">time</text><text x="60" y="12" class="cap">antibodies</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M50,135 q40,-40 80,0" class="pt cool"/><text x="90" y="80" class="cap cool">dead/weak pathogen</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M200,135 q20,-120 60,-110 q40,10 100,40" class="pt hot"/><text x="300" y="20" class="cap hot">real pathogen later</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="290" y="120" class="cap">fast, big: no illness</text></g></svg>

title: Antibiotics and painkillers
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Antibiotics kill bacteria but not viruses; painkillers ease symptoms only"><g class="s1"><rect x="50" y="50" width="26" height="12" rx="6" class="pt"/><rect x="90" y="40" width="26" height="12" rx="6" class="pt"/><rect x="70" y="80" width="26" height="12" rx="6" class="pt"/><rect x="110" y="75" width="26" height="12" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="90" y="115" class="cap">bacteria</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M45,35 L140,100 M140,35 L45,100" class="pt cool"/><text x="90" y="135" class="cap cool">antibiotic kills them</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M220,60 l8,-8 l8,8 l-8,8 z M270,70 l8,-8 l8,8 l-8,8 z" class="pt"/><text x="255" y="115" class="cap hot">viruses: no effect</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="330" y="60" class="cap">painkiller:</text><text x="330" y="76" class="cap">eases symptoms,</text><text x="330" y="92" class="cap">kills nothing</text></g></svg>

title: Testing a new drug
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 130" role="img" aria-label="A new drug is tested on cells and animals, then healthy volunteers at low dose, then patients in a double blind trial"><g class="s1"><rect x="10.5" y="30" width="117" height="40" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="69" y="54" class="cap">lab + animals</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M128.5,50 L140.5,50 M135.2,47.1 L140.5,50 L135.2,52.9" class="pt"/><rect x="141.5" y="30" width="117" height="40" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="54" class="cap">healthy, low dose</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M259.5,50 L271.5,50 M266.2,47.1 L271.5,50 L266.2,52.9" class="pt"/><rect x="272.5" y="30" width="117" height="40" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="331" y="54" class="cap">patients, blind</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="100" class="cap">checks toxicity, efficacy and dose</text><text x="200" y="118" class="cap">placebo group: neither patient nor doctor knows</text></g></svg>

title: Making monoclonal antibodies
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="A mouse lymphocyte fuses with a tumour cell to make a hybridoma, which divides and makes one antibody"><g class="s1"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="18" class="pt"/><text x="50" y="85" class="cap">lymphocyte</text><circle cx="50" cy="115" r="18" class="pt hot"/><text x="50" y="145" class="cap hot">tumour cell</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M80,80 L130,80 M124.7,77.1 L130,80 L124.7,82.9" class="pt"/><ellipse cx="170" cy="80" rx="34" ry="24" class="pt"/><text x="170" y="84" class="cap">hybridoma</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="240" cy="60" r="11" class="pt mv-pulse"/><circle cx="266" cy="60" r="11" class="pt mv-pulse"/><circle cx="240" cy="86" r="11" class="pt mv-pulse"/><circle cx="266" cy="86" r="11" class="pt mv-pulse"/><text x="255" y="125" class="cap">clones</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M330,50 v10 M330,50 l-6,-7 M330,50 l6,-7" class="pt cool mv-jig"/><path d="M350,80 v10 M350,80 l-6,-7 M350,80 l6,-7" class="pt cool mv-jig"/><path d="M325,105 v10 M325,105 l-6,-7 M325,105 l6,-7" class="pt cool mv-jig"/><text x="340" y="140" class="cap cool">one antibody</text></g></svg>

title: Pregnancy test
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 140" role="img" aria-label="Urine moves along a stick; HCG binds to monoclonal antibodies and a coloured line shows a positive test"><g class="s1"><rect x="20" y="55" width="360" height="30" rx="10" class="pt"/><text x="50" y="110" class="cap">urine in</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M40,70 L130,70 M124.7,67.1 L130,70 L124.7,72.9" class="pt mv-flow"/><circle cx="110" cy="70" r="4" class="fill hot"/><text x="110" y="45" class="cap hot">HCG hormone</text></g><g class="s3"><line x1="220" y1="58" x2="220" y2="82" class="pt hot"/><text x="220" y="110" class="cap hot">antibodies trap HCG: line</text></g><g class="s4"><line x1="320" y1="58" x2="320" y2="82" class="pt"/><text x="320" y="130" class="cap">control line</text></g></svg>

title: Detection and identification of plant diseases
subject: Biology

title: Ion deficiency
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="A healthy plant beside a stunted nitrate-deficient plant and a yellow-leaved magnesium-deficient plant"><g class="s1"><line x1="70" y1="140" x2="70" y2="40" class="pt cool"/><ellipse cx="50" cy="60" rx="18" ry="8" class="pt cool"/><ellipse cx="90" cy="80" rx="18" ry="8" class="pt cool"/><text x="70" y="158" class="cap">healthy</text></g><g class="s2"><line x1="200" y1="140" x2="200" y2="105" class="pt"/><ellipse cx="186" cy="112" rx="10" ry="5" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="158" class="cap">no nitrate: stunted</text></g><g class="s3"><line x1="330" y1="140" x2="330" y2="40" class="pt"/><ellipse cx="310" cy="60" rx="18" ry="8" class="pt mv-pulse"/><ellipse cx="350" cy="80" rx="18" ry="8" class="pt mv-pulse"/><text x="330" y="158" class="cap">no Mg: yellow leaves</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="20" class="cap">nitrate → protein · magnesium → chlorophyll</text></g></svg>

title: Plant defences
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Plants defend themselves with a waxy cuticle and cell walls, chemicals, and thorns"><g class="s1"><path d="M40,120 V30" class="pt cool"/><path d="M40,60 l-10,-8 M40,90 l10,-8 M40,45 l10,-6" class="pt cool"/><text x="75" y="135" class="cap">thorns (mechanical)</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="130" y="40" width="100" height="50" rx="4" class="pt cool"/><rect x="125" y="35" width="110" height="60" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="165" y="115" class="cap">waxy cuticle, cell wall</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="324" cy="49" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="332" cy="67" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="310" cy="65" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="298" cy="64" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="302" cy="55" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="317" cy="72" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><text x="325" y="115" class="cap">antibacterial chemicals</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="162" class="cap">barriers stop pathogens getting in</text></g></svg>

title: Photosynthesis
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Carbon dioxide and water enter a leaf; light is absorbed by chlorophyll; glucose and oxygen are made"><g class="s1"><path d="M120,90 q80,-70 160,0 q-80,70 -160,0 z" class="pt cool"/><text x="200" y="94" class="cap cool">chloroplast</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M60,10 L130,60 M127.4,54.6 L130,60 L124.0,59.3" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><path d="M100,5 L160,55 M157.8,49.4 L160,55 L154.1,53.8" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="60" y="25" class="cap hot">light</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M40,100 L115,95 M109.6,92.5 L115,95 L109.9,98.2" class="pt"/><text x="50" y="125" class="cap">CO₂ + water</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M285,90 L360,90 M354.7,87.1 L360,90 L354.7,92.9" class="pt"/><text x="330" y="80" class="cap">glucose + O₂</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="160" class="cap">endothermic: energy taken in</text></g></svg>

title: Limiting factors
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Rate of photosynthesis rises with light intensity, then levels off when another factor is limiting"><g class="s1"><path d="M40,15 V140 H380" class="pt"/><text x="210" y="160" class="cap">light intensity</text><text x="60" y="12" class="cap">rate</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M40,140 L180,50" class="pt hot"/><text x="100" y="70" class="cap hot">light limits</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M180,50 Q220,38 370,38" class="pt cool"/><text x="290" y="28" class="cap cool">CO₂ or temperature limits</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M180,50 Q230,10 370,8" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="290" y="120" class="cap">more CO₂: higher plateau</text></g></svg>

title: Uses of glucose
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Glucose from photosynthesis is used for respiration, starch, fat, cellulose and amino acids"><g class="s1"><circle cx="200" cy="85" r="28" class="pt mv-pulse"/><text x="200" y="89" class="cap">glucose</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M172,75 L90,30 M93.2,35.1 L90,30 L96.0,30.0" class="pt"/><text x="60" y="25" class="cap">respiration</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M228,75 L310,30 M304.0,30.0 L310,30 L306.8,35.1" class="pt"/><text x="340" y="25" class="cap">starch (store)</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M172,95 L90,140 M96.0,140.0 L90,140 L93.2,134.9" class="pt"/><text x="60" y="155" class="cap">fat or oil</text></g><g class="s5"><path d="M228,95 L310,140 M306.8,134.9 L310,140 L304.0,140.0" class="pt"/><text x="340" y="155" class="cap">cellulose walls</text></g><g class="s6"><path d="M200,113 L200,140 M202.9,134.7 L200,140 L197.1,134.7" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="158" class="cap">+ nitrate: amino acids</text></g></svg>

title: Aerobic and anaerobic
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and releases much energy; anaerobic respiration makes lactic acid in muscle or ethanol in yeast"><g class="s1"><text x="200" y="20" class="cap">aerobic: glucose + oxygen → CO₂ + water</text><rect x="60" y="30" width="280" height="16" rx="3" class="pt hot"/><rect x="60" y="30" width="280" height="16" rx="3" class="pt hot mv-pulse" style="opacity:.4"/></g><g class="s2"><text x="200" y="70" class="cap">anaerobic (muscle): glucose → lactic acid</text><rect x="60" y="80" width="40" height="16" rx="3" class="pt hot"/></g><g class="s3"><text x="200" y="120" class="cap">yeast/plants: glucose → ethanol + CO₂</text><rect x="60" y="128" width="40" height="16" rx="3" class="pt hot"/></g><g class="s4"><text x="270" y="145" class="cap hot">bar = energy released</text></g></svg>

title: Oxygen debt
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Breathing rate rises during exercise and stays high afterwards to repay the oxygen debt"><g class="s1"><path d="M40,15 V140 H380" class="pt"/><text x="210" y="160" class="cap">time</text><text x="80" y="12" class="cap">breathing rate</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="110" y="15" width="120" height="125" rx="0" class="pt" style="stroke-dasharray:2 4"/><text x="170" y="30" class="cap">exercise</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M40,120 H110 Q130,50 230,50" class="pt hot"/></g><g class="s4"><path d="M230,50 Q270,55 300,110 T370,120" class="pt hot"/><text x="300" y="70" class="cap">oxygen debt repaid</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="300" y="92" class="cap hot">lactic acid → liver</text></g></svg>

title: Metabolism
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Energy from respiration builds big molecules from small ones and breaks excess protein down to urea"><g class="s1"><text x="200" y="20" class="cap hot">energy from respiration drives:</text></g><g class="s2"><text x="200" y="54" class="cap">glucose → starch, glycogen, cellulose</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="200" y="84" class="cap">glycerol + 3 fatty acids → lipid</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="114" class="cap">glucose + nitrate → amino acids → protein</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="144" class="cap hot">excess protein → urea</text></g></svg>

title: A control system
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 130" role="img" aria-label="A change is detected by a receptor, processed by a coordination centre and corrected by an effector"><g class="s1"><rect x="12" y="30" width="64" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="44" y="51" class="cap">change</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M77,47 L89,47 M83.7,44.1 L89,47 L83.7,49.9" class="pt"/><rect x="90" y="30" width="64" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="122" y="51" class="cap">receptor</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M155,47 L167,47 M161.7,44.1 L167,47 L161.7,49.9" class="pt"/><rect x="168" y="30" width="64" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="51" class="cap">centre</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M233,47 L245,47 M239.7,44.1 L245,47 L239.7,49.9" class="pt"/><rect x="246" y="30" width="64" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="278" y="51" class="cap">effector</text></g><g class="s5"><path d="M311,47 L323,47 M317.7,44.1 L323,47 L317.7,49.9" class="pt"/><rect x="324" y="30" width="64" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="356" y="51" class="cap">response</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="200" y="22" class="cap">coordination</text></g><g class="s6"><path d="M360,64 V100 H40 V64" class="pt cool mv-flow"/><text x="200" y="120" class="cap cool">keeps conditions steady</text></g></svg>

title: The reflex arc
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="Stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone in the spinal cord, motor neurone, effector"><g class="s1"><text x="40" y="30" class="cap">stimulus</text><circle cx="40" cy="55" r="8" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><text x="40" y="80" class="cap">receptor</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M50,55 H160" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="105" y="45" class="cap">sensory</text></g><g class="s3"><rect x="160" y="30" width="80" height="90" rx="10" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="135" class="cap">spinal cord</text><path d="M170,55 V95 H230" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="200" y="75" class="cap">relay</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M240,95 H350" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="295" y="85" class="cap">motor</text></g><g class="s5"><rect x="350" y="80" width="40" height="30" rx="6" class="pt mv-pulse"/><text x="370" y="130" class="cap">muscle</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="155" class="cap">fast and automatic: no thinking</text></g></svg>

title: Parts of the brain
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="The cerebral cortex, cerebellum and medulla and what each controls"><g class="s1"><path d="M80,110 Q60,30 170,25 Q290,25 280,100 Q240,110 200,105 Q150,120 80,110 z" class="pt"/><text x="180" y="60" class="cap">cerebral cortex</text><text x="180" y="76" class="cap">thinking, memory, language</text></g><g class="s2"><ellipse cx="260" cy="118" rx="30" ry="16" class="pt mv-pulse"/><text x="330" y="140" class="cap">cerebellum: balance</text></g><g class="s3"><rect x="200" y="105" width="18" height="45" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="150" y="150" class="cap">medulla: heartbeat, breathing</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="330" y="30" class="cap">mapped by MRI,</text><text x="330" y="46" class="cap">damage, stimulation</text></g></svg>

title: Accommodation
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="Light passes the cornea and lens to focus on the retina; for a near object the lens gets fatter"><g class="s1"><circle cx="240" cy="80" r="65" class="pt"/><text x="330" y="30" class="cap">retina</text><path d="M300,40 A65,65 0 0 1 300,120" class="pt hot"/></g><g class="s2"><ellipse cx="185" cy="80" rx="7" ry="28" class="pt"/><text x="185" y="125" class="cap">lens</text><path d="M178,40 A70,70 0 0 0 178,120" class="pt"/><text x="160" y="30" class="cap">cornea</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M20,60 L180,60 M174.7,57.1 L180,60 L174.7,62.9" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><path d="M20,100 L180,100 M174.7,97.1 L180,100 L174.7,102.9" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><path d="M190,60 L304,80 M190,100 L304,80" class="pt hot"/></g><g class="s4"><g class="mv-pulse"><ellipse cx="185" cy="80" rx="12" ry="28" class="pt cool"/></g><text x="200" y="155" class="cap cool">near: ciliary muscles contract, lens fatter</text></g></svg>

title: Body temperature
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="Too hot: vessels dilate and you sweat; too cold: vessels constrict and you shiver"><g class="s1"><circle cx="200" cy="30" r="18" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="34" class="cap">brain</text><text x="200" y="64" class="cap">thermoregulatory centre</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M180,72 L100,95 M105.9,96.3 L100,95 L104.3,90.8" class="pt hot"/><text x="90" y="90" class="cap hot">too hot</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M30,115 H170 M30,135 H170" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="60" cy="108" r="3" class="fill mv-jig cool"/><circle cx="120" cy="108" r="3" class="fill mv-jig cool"/><text x="100" y="155" class="cap hot">vasodilation, sweat</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M220,72 L300,95 M295.7,90.8 L300,95 L294.1,96.3" class="pt cool"/><text x="310" y="90" class="cap cool">too cold</text></g><g class="s5"><path d="M230,120 H370 M230,130 H370" class="pt cool"/><path d="M300,105 l-4,4 l8,0 l-4,4" class="pt mv-jig"/><text x="300" y="155" class="cap cool">vasoconstriction, shiver</text></g></svg>

title: Endocrine glands
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 200" role="img" aria-label="The pituitary, thyroid, adrenal glands, pancreas, ovaries and testes release hormones into the blood"><g class="s1"><circle cx="200" cy="30" r="20" class="pt"/><path d="M200,50 V60 M170,60 H230 L220,150 H180 Z" class="pt"/><text x="80" y="20" class="cap">endocrine glands</text></g><g class="s2"><circle cx="200" cy="36" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><text x="290" y="36" class="cap">pituitary: master gland</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="200" cy="60" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><text x="290" y="62" class="cap">thyroid</text></g><g class="s4"><circle cx="188" cy="100" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><circle cx="212" cy="100" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><text x="290" y="100" class="cap">adrenal</text></g><g class="s5"><circle cx="200" cy="115" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><text x="290" y="118" class="cap">pancreas</text></g><g class="s6"><circle cx="190" cy="140" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><circle cx="210" cy="140" r="4" class="fill hot mv-pulse"/><text x="290" y="142" class="cap">ovaries / testes</text></g><g class="s7"><text x="200" y="185" class="cap">hormones travel in the blood to target organs</text></g></svg>

title: Blood glucose
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 158" role="img" aria-label="Blood glucose rises after a meal; the pancreas releases insulin and the liver stores glucose as glycogen"><g class="s1"><text x="60" y="20" class="cap">after a meal</text><path d="M60,70 L60,30 M57.1,35.3 L60,30 L62.9,35.3" class="pt hot"/><text x="60" y="90" class="cap hot">glucose high</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="120" y="40" width="70" height="30" rx="12" class="pt"/><text x="155" y="60" class="cap">pancreas</text><path d="M190,55 L250,55 M244.7,52.1 L250,55 L244.7,57.9" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="220" y="45" class="cap">insulin</text></g><g class="s3"><rect x="255" y="35" width="80" height="40" rx="14" class="pt"/><text x="295" y="59" class="cap">liver, cells</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="295" y="95" class="cap cool">glucose → glycogen</text><path d="M60,110 L60,140 M62.9,134.7 L60,140 L57.1,134.7" class="pt cool"/><text x="150" y="130" class="cap cool">glucose back to normal</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="295" y="148" class="cap">HT: glucagon does the reverse</text></g></svg>

title: Maintaining water and nitrogen balance in the body
subject: Biology

title: The kidney
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="The kidney filters blood and reabsorbs glucose, some ions and some water; ADH controls how much water is reabsorbed"><g class="s1"><path d="M120,30 q-60,0 -60,60 t60,60 q30,0 30,-30 q-20,-30 0,-60 q0,-30 -30,-30 z" class="pt"/><text x="100" y="155" class="cap">kidney</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M10,60 L70,60 M64.7,57.1 L70,60 L64.7,62.9" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="30" y="50" class="cap hot">blood in</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="270" y="30" class="cap">filter: small molecules out</text><text x="270" y="55" class="cap cool">reabsorb: all glucose,</text><text x="270" y="71" class="cap cool">some ions, some water</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M150,120 L200,140 M196.2,135.4 L200,140 L194.0,140.7" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="250" y="145" class="cap">urine: urea, excess water and ions</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="270" y="105" class="cap hot">ADH from pituitary: keep more water</text></g></svg>

title: The menstrual cycle
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Over 28 days FSH matures an egg, oestrogen builds the lining, LH triggers ovulation at about day 14, progesterone keeps the lining"><g class="s1"><path d="M30,140 H380" class="pt"/><text x="30" y="158" class="cap">0</text><text x="205" y="158" class="cap">14</text><text x="372" y="158" class="cap">28 d</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M30,120 q40,-50 90,-10 T200,130" class="pt cool"/><text x="60" y="75" class="cap cool">FSH</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M30,130 Q150,40 200,60 T380,110" class="pt hot"/><text x="140" y="55" class="cap hot">oestrogen</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M170,135 L200,30 L230,135" class="pt"/><text x="225" y="25" class="cap">LH: ovulation</text></g><g class="s5"><path d="M210,135 Q290,40 380,130" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="320" y="60" class="cap">progesterone</text></g></svg>

title: Contraception
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Hormonal methods stop eggs maturing; barrier and other methods stop sperm reaching an egg"><g class="s1"><circle cx="320" cy="75" r="22" class="pt"/><text x="320" y="79" class="cap">egg</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:120px"><ellipse cx="40" cy="60" rx="6" ry="4" class="pt"/><path d="M34,60 h-14" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:120px"><ellipse cx="60" cy="85" rx="6" ry="4" class="pt"/><path d="M54,85 h-14" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:120px"><ellipse cx="35" cy="105" rx="6" ry="4" class="pt"/><path d="M29,105 h-14" class="pt"/></g></g><g class="s3"><line x1="220" y1="30" x2="220" y2="120" class="pt hot"/><text x="220" y="140" class="cap hot">barrier: condom, diaphragm</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="320" y="20" class="cap cool">hormones: no egg matures</text><path d="M302,57 L338,93 M338,57 L302,93" class="pt cool"/></g></svg>

title: The use of hormones to treat infertility
subject: Biology

title: IVF
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 120" role="img" aria-label="FSH and LH are given, eggs are collected and fertilised in the lab, and embryos are put into the uterus"><g class="s1"><rect x="11.5" y="30" width="69" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="46" y="52" class="cap">FSH, LH</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M81.5,48 L87.5,48 M82.2,45.1 L87.5,48 L82.2,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="88.5" y="30" width="69" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="123" y="52" class="cap">eggs out</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M158.5,48 L164.5,48 M159.2,45.1 L164.5,48 L159.2,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="165.5" y="30" width="69" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="52" class="cap">fertilise</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M235.5,48 L241.5,48 M236.2,45.1 L241.5,48 L236.2,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="242.5" y="30" width="69" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="277" y="52" class="cap">embryo</text></g><g class="s5"><path d="M312.5,48 L318.5,48 M313.2,45.1 L318.5,48 L313.2,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="319.5" y="30" width="69" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="354" y="52" class="cap">to uterus</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="100" class="cap hot">costly, stressful, low success; risk of multiple births</text></g></svg>

title: Negative feedback
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="The pituitary releases TSH, the thyroid makes thyroxine, high thyroxine lowers TSH"><g class="s1"><rect x="40" y="30" width="110" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="95" y="51" class="cap">pituitary</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M150,47 L240,47 M234.7,44.1 L240,47 L234.7,49.9" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="195" y="38" class="cap">TSH</text><rect x="245" y="30" width="110" height="34" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="300" y="51" class="cap">thyroid</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M300,64 V110 H95 V70" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="200" y="125" class="cap hot">high thyroxine</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="95" y="90" class="cap hot">− less TSH</text><text x="200" y="145" class="cap">so the level falls back to normal</text></g></svg>

title: Phototropism
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="Light from one side; auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows more, so the shoot bends towards the light"><g class="s1"><path d="M20,50 L90,50 M84.7,47.1 L90,50 L84.7,52.9" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="40" y="35" class="cap hot">light</text><path d="M150,150 H250" class="pt"/></g><g class="s2"><rect x="190" y="60" width="20" height="90" rx="4" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="50" class="cap">shoot</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="206" cy="75" r="3" class="fill mv-jig cool"/><circle cx="206" cy="95" r="3" class="fill mv-jig cool"/><circle cx="206" cy="115" r="3" class="fill mv-jig cool"/><text x="300" y="100" class="cap cool">auxin on shaded side</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M200,150 Q200,80 150,40" class="pt cool"/><text x="305" y="120" class="cap">shaded side grows more</text><text x="305" y="136" class="cap">so it bends to light</text></g></svg>

title: Using plant hormones
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Auxins kill weeds and root cuttings; gibberellins end seed dormancy and make bigger fruit; ethene ripens fruit"><g class="s1"><text x="80" y="25" class="cap">auxins</text><text x="95" y="45" class="cap">weedkiller, rooting powder</text></g><g class="s2"><text x="310" y="25" class="cap">gibberellins</text><text x="305" y="45" class="cap">seeds sprout, bigger fruit</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="200" cy="105" r="20" class="pt cool mv-pulse"/><text x="200" y="145" class="cap">ethene: ripens fruit in transit</text></g><g class="s4"><circle cx="200" cy="105" r="20" class="pt hot" style="opacity:.6"/></g></svg>

title: Sexual and asexual reproduction
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Two gametes fuse to make varied offspring; one parent divides by mitosis to make identical clones"><g class="s1"><circle cx="50" cy="40" r="12" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="110" cy="40" r="8" class="pt cool"/><path d="M60,55 L75,80 M74.8,74.0 L75,80 L69.8,77.0" class="pt"/><path d="M105,50 L90,80 M94.9,76.6 L90,80 L89.8,74.0" class="pt"/><text x="80" y="20" class="cap">two gametes</text></g><g class="s2"><circle cx="80" cy="100" r="16" class="pt"/><text x="80" y="138" class="cap">varied offspring</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="300" cy="40" r="16" class="pt"/><text x="300" y="20" class="cap">one parent: mitosis</text><path d="M290,58 L260,85 M265.8,83.6 L260,85 L262.0,79.3" class="pt"/><path d="M310,58 L340,85 M338.0,79.3 L340,85 L334.2,83.6" class="pt"/></g><g class="s4"><circle cx="255" cy="100" r="14" class="pt"/><circle cx="345" cy="100" r="14" class="pt"/><text x="300" y="138" class="cap">identical clones</text></g></svg>

title: Meiosis
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="A cell copies its chromosomes and divides twice to make four gametes, each with one set"><g class="s1"><circle cx="60" cy="85" r="30" class="pt"/><path d="M44,74 l4,22 M52,74 l-4,22" class="pt"/><path d="M62,74 l4,22 M70,74 l-4,22" class="pt hot"/><text x="60" y="135" class="cap">copies chromosomes</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M95,70 L140,50 M134.0,49.5 L140,50 L136.4,54.8" class="pt"/><path d="M95,100 L140,120 M136.4,115.2 L140,120 L134.0,120.5" class="pt"/><circle cx="165" cy="45" r="20" class="pt"/><circle cx="165" cy="125" r="20" class="pt"/><path d="M161,34 l4,22 M169,34 l-4,22" class="pt"/><path d="M161,114 l4,22 M169,114 l-4,22" class="pt hot"/><text x="165" y="160" class="cap">divide once</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="260" cy="25" r="15" class="pt mv-pulse"/><line x1="258" y1="17" x2="262" y2="33" class="pt"/><circle cx="260" cy="70" r="15" class="pt mv-pulse"/><line x1="258" y1="62" x2="262" y2="78" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="260" cy="105" r="15" class="pt mv-pulse"/><line x1="258" y1="97" x2="262" y2="113" class="pt"/><circle cx="260" cy="150" r="15" class="pt mv-pulse"/><line x1="258" y1="142" x2="262" y2="158" class="pt hot"/><path d="M188,45 L240,30 M234.1,28.7 L240,30 L235.7,34.2" class="pt"/><path d="M188,125 L240,145 M236.1,140.4 L240,145 L234.1,145.8" class="pt"/></g><g class="s4"><text x="340" y="70" class="cap">four gametes,</text><text x="340" y="86" class="cap">one set each,</text><text x="340" y="102" class="cap">all different</text></g></svg>

title: Advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction
subject: Biology

title: Sexual versus asexual
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Sexual reproduction gives variation; asexual is faster, needs one parent and makes many identical offspring"><g class="s1"><text x="100" y="25" class="cap">sexual</text><line x1="200" y1="15" x2="200" y2="140" class="pt"/></g><g class="s2"><text x="100" y="55" class="cap cool">variation: survive change</text><text x="100" y="75" class="cap cool">selective breeding</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="300" y="25" class="cap">asexual</text><text x="300" y="55" class="cap cool">one parent, fast</text><text x="300" y="75" class="cap cool">many copies when good</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="120" class="cap">both: malaria parasite, fungi, strawberries, daffodils</text></g></svg>

title: Variation
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="A bell-shaped spread of heights in a population, caused by genes and the environment"><g class="s1"><path d="M30,130 H370" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="150" class="cap">height</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="50" y="120" width="26" height="10" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="80" y="105" width="26" height="25" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="110" y="85" width="26" height="45" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="140" y="60" width="26" height="70" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="170" y="35" width="26" height="95" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="200" y="35" width="26" height="95" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="230" y="60" width="26" height="70" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="260" y="85" width="26" height="45" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="290" y="105" width="26" height="25" rx="0" class="pt"/><rect x="320" y="120" width="26" height="10" rx="0" class="pt"/></g><g class="s3"><text x="90" y="30" class="cap cool">genes</text><text x="310" y="30" class="cap hot">environment</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="18" class="cap">most variation: both together</text></g></svg>

title: Natural selection
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="In a population that varies, the best suited survive and breed; over generations their alleles become common"><g class="s1"><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="10" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="68" cy="50" r="10" class="pt"/><circle cx="96" cy="50" r="10" class="pt"/><circle cx="124" cy="50" r="10" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="152" cy="50" r="10" class="pt"/><circle cx="180" cy="50" r="10" class="pt"/><text x="110" y="85" class="cap">variation</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M210,50 L240,50 M234.7,47.1 L240,50 L234.7,52.9" class="pt"/><circle cx="260" cy="50" r="10" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="288" cy="50" r="10" class="pt hot"/><circle cx="316" cy="50" r="10" class="pt"/><text x="290" y="85" class="cap">best suited survive</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M290,95 L290,110 M292.9,104.7 L290,110 L287.1,104.7" class="pt"/><circle cx="150" cy="125" r="10" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><circle cx="178" cy="125" r="10" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><circle cx="206" cy="125" r="10" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><circle cx="234" cy="125" r="10" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><circle cx="262" cy="125" r="10" class="pt"/><circle cx="290" cy="125" r="10" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><text x="230" y="155" class="cap">alleles passed on: become common</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="60" y="125" class="cap">many generations</text></g></svg>

title: Selective breeding
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 120" role="img" aria-label="Choose parents with the wanted trait, breed them, choose the best offspring, repeat over many generations"><g class="s1"><rect x="11" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="53" y="52" class="cap">choose parents</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M96,48 L108,48 M102.7,45.1 L108,48 L102.7,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="109" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="151" y="52" class="cap">breed them</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M194,48 L206,48 M200.7,45.1 L206,48 L200.7,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="207" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="249" y="52" class="cap">pick best offspring</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M292,48 L304,48 M298.7,45.1 L304,48 L298.7,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="305" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="347" y="52" class="cap">repeat</text></g><g class="s5"><path d="M355,66 V90 H45 V66" class="pt mv-flow"/><text x="200" y="110" class="cap hot">risk: inbreeding</text></g></svg>

title: Genetic engineering
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="A gene is cut out with enzymes, put into a plasmid and carried into bacteria that then make insulin"><g class="s1"><path d="M20,40 H200" class="pt mv-flow"/><rect x="80" y="32" width="40" height="16" rx="0" class="pt hot"/><text x="100" y="22" class="cap hot">insulin gene</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M80,55 v-30 M120,55 v-30" class="pt cool"/><text x="100" y="70" class="cap cool">cut with enzymes</text></g><g class="s3"><circle cx="290" cy="50" r="32" class="pt"/><rect x="275" y="12" width="30" height="12" rx="0" class="pt hot"/><text x="290" y="100" class="cap">into a plasmid (vector)</text></g><g class="s4"><rect x="200" y="115" width="110" height="34" rx="17" class="pt"/><circle cx="255" cy="132" r="8" class="pt"/><text x="345" y="136" class="cap">bacteria</text><circle cx="220" cy="160" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/><circle cx="300" cy="160" r="2.5" class="fill mv-jig hot"/></g><g class="s5"><text x="120" y="135" class="cap hot">make human insulin</text></g></svg>

title: Adult cell cloning
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="A body cell nucleus goes into an egg cell with no nucleus; an electric shock starts division; the embryo is implanted"><g class="s1"><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="22" class="pt"/><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="8" class="fill"/><text x="50" y="95" class="cap">body nucleus</text></g><g class="s2"><circle cx="160" cy="50" r="26" class="pt"/><path d="M150,40 l20,20 M170,40 l-20,20" class="pt hot"/><text x="160" y="95" class="cap">egg, nucleus out</text></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:120px"><circle cx="40" cy="50" r="8" class="fill"/></g><path d="M200,20 l-8,14 h10 l-8,14" class="pt hot mv-pulse"/><text x="200" y="120" class="cap">electric shock: divides</text></g><g class="s4"><circle cx="330" cy="50" r="24" class="pt"/><circle cx="322" cy="44" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="338" cy="44" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="322" cy="58" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="338" cy="58" r="6" class="pt"/><text x="330" y="95" class="cap">embryo → host</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="142" class="cap">clone: identical to the body cell donor</text></g></svg>

title: Darwin and Lamarck
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Darwin: variation and natural selection; Lamarck wrongly thought changes in a lifetime are passed on"><g class="s1"><text x="100" y="20" class="cap">Darwin</text><line x1="200" y1="10" x2="200" y2="135" class="pt"/></g><g class="s2"><text x="100" y="50" class="cap">variation</text><text x="100" y="70" class="cap">struggle to survive</text><text x="100" y="90" class="cap">fittest breed</text><text x="100" y="110" class="cap">pass on traits</text><text x="100" y="130" class="cap cool">accepted</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="300" y="20" class="cap">Lamarck</text><text x="300" y="60" class="cap">use it in life → inherit it</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="300" y="100" class="cap hot">wrong: acquired changes</text><text x="300" y="118" class="cap hot">are not inherited</text></g></svg>

title: Speciation
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="A population is split by a river; the two groups evolve separately until they can no longer interbreed"><g class="s1"><circle cx="47" cy="46" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="116" cy="45" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="265" cy="54" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="195" cy="87" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="314" cy="40" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="185" cy="90" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="265" cy="67" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="131" cy="60" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="328" cy="39" r="6" class="pt"/><circle cx="369" cy="68" r="6" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="20" class="cap">one population</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M200,0 q-20,40 0,75 t0,75" class="pt cool mv-flow"/><text x="200" y="145" class="cap cool">isolated by a barrier</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="100" y="115" class="cap">evolve separately</text><text x="300" y="115" class="cap">evolve separately</text></g><g class="s4"><rect x="54" y="54" width="12" height="12" rx="0" class="pt hot"/><rect x="114" y="39" width="12" height="12" rx="0" class="pt hot"/><rect x="84" y="74" width="12" height="12" rx="0" class="pt hot"/><text x="300" y="130" class="cap hot">cannot interbreed: new species</text></g></svg>

title: Mendel to DNA
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 120" role="img" aria-label="Mendel’s peas, then chromosomes seen, then genes on chromosomes, then the structure of DNA"><g class="s1"><rect x="11" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="53" y="52" class="cap">Mendel: units</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M96,48 L108,48 M102.7,45.1 L108,48 L102.7,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="109" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="151" y="52" class="cap">chromosomes seen</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M194,48 L206,48 M200.7,45.1 L206,48 L200.7,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="207" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="249" y="52" class="cap">genes on them</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M292,48 L304,48 M298.7,45.1 L304,48 L298.7,50.9" class="pt"/><rect x="305" y="30" width="84" height="36" rx="6" class="pt"/><text x="347" y="52" class="cap">DNA structure</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="100" class="cap">1860s pea plants → mid-20th century DNA</text></g></svg>

title: Evidence for evolution

html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 160" role="img" aria-label="Prey numbers rise and fall; predator numbers follow behind them"><g class="s1"><path d="M30,15 V135 H380" class="pt"/><text x="210" y="152" class="cap">time</text><text x="70" y="12" class="cap">number</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M30,90 C70,10 110,10 150,90 S230,170 270,90 S350,10 380,60" class="pt cool"/><text x="100" y="30" class="cap cool">prey</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M30,115 C90,50 130,50 190,115 S270,170 310,110 S370,60 380,70" class="pt hot"/><text x="210" y="70" class="cap hot">predator lags behind</text></g></svg>

title: Changing distribution
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="As the climate warms a species moves north; changes can be seasonal, geographic or human-made"><g class="s1"><rect x="140" y="10" width="120" height="130" rx="0" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="150" class="cap">map</text><text x="280" y="20" class="cap">north</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--y:-60px"><circle cx="170" cy="110" r="5" class="fill hot"/><circle cx="200" cy="120" r="5" class="fill hot"/><circle cx="230" cy="105" r="5" class="fill hot"/></g></g><g class="s3"><text x="70" y="60" class="cap hot">warmer climate</text><text x="70" y="80" class="cap">→ species moves</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="330" y="70" class="cap">seasonal</text><text x="330" y="90" class="cap">geographic</text><text x="330" y="110" class="cap">human-made</text></g></svg>

title: Pollution

title: Land use
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Land is taken for building, quarrying, farming and waste; draining peat bogs releases carbon dioxide"><g class="s1"><rect x="20" y="30" width="360" height="80" rx="4" class="pt cool"/><text x="200" y="22" class="cap cool">habitat</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="30" y="50" width="50" height="50" rx="0" class="pt"/><path d="M30,50 l25,-15 l25,15" class="pt"/><text x="55" y="125" class="cap">building</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M110,100 l20,-40 h40 l20,40" class="pt"/><text x="150" y="125" class="cap">quarry</text><path d="M220,60 H300 M220,75 H300 M220,90 H300" class="pt"/><text x="260" y="125" class="cap">farm</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M340,90 L340,40 M337.1,45.3 L340,40 L342.9,45.3" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="335" y="125" class="cap hot">peat drained → CO₂</text></g></svg>

title: Deforestation
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Forest is cleared for cattle, rice and biofuel crops; burning releases carbon dioxide and fewer trees take it in"><g class="s1"><line x1="50" y1="120" x2="50" y2="90" class="pt"/><circle cx="50" cy="78" r="14" class="pt cool"/><line x1="90" y1="120" x2="90" y2="90" class="pt"/><circle cx="90" cy="78" r="14" class="pt cool"/><line x1="130" y1="120" x2="130" y2="90" class="pt"/><circle cx="130" cy="78" r="14" class="pt cool"/><line x1="170" y1="120" x2="170" y2="90" class="pt"/><circle cx="170" cy="78" r="14" class="pt cool"/><text x="110" y="140" class="cap cool">tropical forest</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M210,120 H380" class="pt"/><path d="M250,120 l10,-30 l10,30" class="pt"/><text x="300" y="140" class="cap">cattle, rice, biofuel</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M260,80 q-10,-15 0,-25 q10,-10 0,-25" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="300" y="20" class="cap hot">burning: more CO₂</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="300" y="50" class="cap">fewer trees: less CO₂ taken in</text><text x="300" y="66" class="cap">less biodiversity</text></g></svg>

title: Global warming
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="More carbon dioxide and methane trap heat; sea levels rise and species move or are lost"><g class="s1"><path d="M20,40 H380" class="pt hot mv-flow"/><text x="200" y="30" class="cap hot">more CO₂ and methane</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M60,120 L100,50 M94.9,53.1 L100,50 L99.9,56.0" class="pt hot"/><path d="M100,50 L140,120 M139.9,114.0 L140,120 L134.9,116.9" class="pt hot"/><text x="100" y="135" class="cap">heat trapped</text></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-slide" style="--y:-15px"><path d="M200,120 q20,-6 40,0 t40,0 t40,0" class="pt cool"/></g><text x="260" y="140" class="cap cool">sea level rises</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="300" y="70" class="cap">species move, migrate</text><text x="300" y="86" class="cap">or are lost</text></g></svg>

title: Maintaining biodiversity
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Breeding programmes, protected habitats, hedgerows and field margins, less deforestation and recycling"><g class="s1"><text x="100" y="25" class="cap">breeding programmes</text><circle cx="100" cy="50" r="10" class="pt mv-pulse"/></g><g class="s2"><text x="300" y="25" class="cap cool">protect, regenerate habitats</text><rect x="260" y="40" width="80" height="20" rx="4" class="pt cool"/></g><g class="s3"><path d="M40,100 H160" class="pt cool" style="stroke-width:6"/><text x="100" y="125" class="cap cool">hedgerows, field margins</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="300" y="100" class="cap">less deforestation, less CO₂</text><text x="300" y="125" class="cap">recycle, not landfill</text></g></svg>

title: Trophic levels

title: Pyramid of biomass
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 150" role="img" aria-label="Bars drawn to scale: producers widest at the bottom, each level above smaller"><g class="s1"><rect x="40" y="110" width="320" height="28" rx="0" class="pt cool"/><text x="200" y="129" class="cap cool">producers 1000 g</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="150" y="80" width="100" height="28" rx="0" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="99" class="cap">100 g</text></g><g class="s3"><rect x="185" y="50" width="30" height="28" rx="0" class="pt"/><text x="260" y="69" class="cap">10 g</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="200" y="30" class="cap hot">biomass falls at every level</text></g></svg>

style="fill:var(--bg);font-size:11px;font-weight:700;opacity:1">O 3 × 16</text></g></g><g class="s5"><text class="cap" style="font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;opacity:1;transform:var(--t, none);transform-origin:center;transform-box:fill-box"><tspan x="120" y="202">Carbon adds 12</tspan></text></g></g><text x="240" y="439.6" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">O 3 × 16</text><text x="240" y="462" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">Mr = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100</text><text x="240" y="484.4" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">100 g of CaCO₃ = 1 mole</text><text x="240" y="506.8" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">Its Mr in grams is one mole: 100 g of CaCO₃</text><g class="s1"><text x="240" y="529.2" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">100 = 56 + 44</text></g><g class="s1"><text x="240" y="551.6" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂</text></g><g class="s1"><text x="240" y="574" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">Heated, it splits: 56 + 44 — the mass is conserved</text></g><g class="s2"><text x="240" y="596.4" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">[H] moles = mass ÷ Mr</text></g><g class="s2"><text x="240" y="618.8" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">25 g ÷ 100 = 0.25 mol</text></g><g class="s2"><text x="240" y="641.2" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">25 g is a quarter of 100 g, so a quarter of a mole</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="240" y="663.6" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">Add up the relative atomic masses: calcium is 40</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="240" y="686" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">40 + 12 = 52</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="240" y="708.4" class="cap" style="font-size:14px">Three oxygens add 3 × 16 = 48: Mr of CaCO₃ is 100</text></g></svg>

title: Formulations

title: Chromatography
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Solvent climbs the paper and separates the inks into spots"><g class="s1"><rect x="120" y="20" width="80" height="130" class="pt"/><line x1="120" y1="130" x2="200" y2="130" class="ln" style="stroke-dasharray:3 3"/><rect x="100" y="140" width="120" height="14" class="fill cool" style="opacity:.3"/></g><g class="s2"><circle cx="160" cy="130" r="4" class="fill"/></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-100px"><rect x="121" y="128" width="78" height="2" class="fill cool"/></g><text x="250" y="30" class="cap" text-anchor="start">solvent front</text></g><g class="s4"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-70px"><circle cx="160" cy="130" r="4" class="fill hot"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-35px"><circle cx="160" cy="130" r="4" class="fill" style="fill:#2a6fdb"/></g></g><g class="s5"><text x="270" y="80" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Rf = spot ÷ solvent</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="270" y="105" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">pure: one spot</text></g><g class="s7"><text x="60" y="130" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">start line</text></g></svg>

title: Test for hydrogen
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="A burning splint at the mouth of the tube: a squeaky pop"><g class="s1"><path d="M140 40V130a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><text x="150" y="160" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">hydrogen</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="" style="transform:translate(0px,-10px)"><rect x="148" y="0" width="4" height="50" class="fill" style="fill:#a0763c"/><g class="mv-pulse"><circle cx="150" cy="-4" r="5" class="fill hot"/></g></g></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-pulse"><text x="250" y="40" class="cap hot" text-anchor="middle">POP!</text></g></g><g class="s4"><text x="280" y="90" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">burning splint</text></g></svg>

title: Test for oxygen
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="A glowing splint relights in oxygen"><g class="s1"><path d="M140 40V130a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><text x="150" y="160" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">oxygen</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:40px"><rect x="148" y="0" width="4" height="50" class="fill" style="fill:#a0763c"/><circle cx="150" cy="50" r="3" class="fill hot" style="opacity:.6"/></g></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-pulse"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M142 95q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:var(--coral);opacity:.85"/></g></g></g><g class="s4"><text x="270" y="90" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">glowing splint relights</text></g></svg>

title: Test for carbon dioxide
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Carbon dioxide bubbled through limewater turns it milky"><g class="s1"><path d="M190 40V130a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M191 85V130a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V85Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><text x="200" y="160" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">limewater</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M120 20H200V120" class="pt"/><text x="110" y="40" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">CO₂</text></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="194" cy="125" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="200" cy="119" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="206" cy="113" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="194" cy="107" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="200" cy="101" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="206" cy="95" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g></g><g class="s4"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M191 85V130a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V85Z" class="fill" style="fill:#ddd;opacity:.9"/></g></g><g class="s5"><text x="300" y="90" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">turns milky</text></g></svg>

title: Test for chlorine
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Damp litmus paper is bleached white by chlorine"><g class="s1"><path d="M140 50V140a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V50" class="pt"/><path d="M141 95V140a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V95Z" class="fill" style="fill:#cfe36a;opacity:.8"/><text x="150" y="165" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">chlorine</text></g><g class="s2"><rect x="140" y="10" width="20" height="40" style="fill:#3c7fd0"/></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-pulse"><rect x="140" y="10" width="20" height="40" style="fill:#fff;stroke:#999"/></g></g><g class="s4"><text x="260" y="30" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">damp litmus paper</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="260" y="60" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">bleached white</text></g></svg>

title: Flame tests
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Lithium crimson, sodium yellow, potassium lilac, calcium orange-red, copper green"><g class="s1"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M42 110q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:#b0102f;opacity:.85"/></g><text x="50" y="130" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Li⁺</text><text x="50" y="146" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">crimson</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M117 110q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:#f2c200;opacity:.85"/></g><text x="125" y="130" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Na⁺</text><text x="125" y="146" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">yellow</text></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M192 110q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:#b38ad6;opacity:.85"/></g><text x="200" y="130" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">K⁺</text><text x="200" y="146" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">lilac</text></g><g class="s4"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M267 110q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:#f06a2a;opacity:.85"/></g><text x="275" y="130" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Ca²⁺</text><text x="275" y="146" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">orange-red</text></g><g class="s5"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M342 110q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:#2fb34a;opacity:.85"/></g><text x="350" y="130" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Cu²⁺</text><text x="350" y="146" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">green</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="30" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">a mixture of ions can mask colours</text></g></svg>

title: Metal hydroxide precipitates
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Sodium hydroxide gives coloured precipitates with metal ions"><g class="s1"><path d="M50 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M51 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="60" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#eee"/></g><path d="M51 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#eee"/><text x="60" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Al, Ca, Mg: white</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M150 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M151 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="160" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#2a6fdb"/></g><path d="M151 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#2a6fdb"/><text x="160" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Cu²⁺: blue</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M240 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M241 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="250" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#3a8a3a"/></g><path d="M241 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#3a8a3a"/><text x="250" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Fe²⁺: green</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M330 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M331 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="340" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#8b4513"/></g><path d="M331 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#8b4513"/><text x="340" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Fe³⁺: brown</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="20" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">add sodium hydroxide solution</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="167" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">only the Al³⁺ precipitate dissolves in excess</text></g></svg>

title: Test for carbonates
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Acid on a carbonate gives carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky"><g class="s1"><path d="M90 40V130a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M91 85V130a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V85Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><text x="100" y="160" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">carbonate + dilute acid</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="94" cy="125" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="100" cy="119" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="106" cy="113" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="94" cy="107" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="100" cy="101" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-22px"><circle cx="106" cy="95" r="2.5" class="pt"/></g></g><g class="s3"><path d="M100 40V20H260V60" class="pt"/></g><g class="s4"><path d="M250 50V130a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V50" class="pt"/><path d="M251 90.5V130a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V90.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/></g><g class="s5"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M251 90V130a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V90Z" class="fill" style="fill:#ddd;opacity:.9"/></g><text x="260" y="160" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">limewater turns milky</text></g></svg>

title: Test for halides
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Nitric acid then silver nitrate: white, cream or yellow precipitate"><g class="s1"><text x="200" y="20" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">add dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M90 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M91 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="100" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#f4f4f4"/></g><path d="M91 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#f4f4f4"/><text x="100" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Cl⁻: white</text></g><g class="s3"><path d="M190 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M191 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="200" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#efe3b8"/></g><path d="M191 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#efe3b8"/><text x="200" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Br⁻: cream</text></g><g class="s4"><path d="M290 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M291 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="300" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#f2dc3a"/></g><path d="M291 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#f2dc3a"/><text x="300" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">I⁻: yellow</text></g></svg>

title: Test for sulfates
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Hydrochloric acid then barium chloride: a white precipitate"><g class="s1"><text x="200" y="20" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">add dilute HCl, then barium chloride</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M150 40V120a10 10 0 0 0 20 0V40" class="pt"/><path d="M151 80.5V120a9 9 0 0 0 18 0V80.5Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.35"/><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:50px"><circle cx="160" cy="62" r="3" class="fill" style="fill:#f4f4f4"/></g><path d="M151 118a9 9 0 0 0 18 0Z" style="fill:#f4f4f4"/><text x="160" y="150" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">white precipitate</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="300" y="80" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">barium sulfate</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="300" y="100" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">BaSO₄</text></g></svg>

title: Instrumental methods
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Machines analyse tiny samples quickly and accurately"><g class="s1"><rect x="130" y="50" width="140" height="70" rx="5" class="pt"/><text x="200" y="90" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">instrument</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:70px;--y:0px"><circle cx="60" cy="85" r="3" class="fill hot"/></g><text x="60" y="110" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">tiny sample</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="330" y="60" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">accurate</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="330" y="85" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">sensitive</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="330" y="110" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">rapid</text></g></svg>

title: Flame emission spectroscopy
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Light from a flame is split into a line spectrum to identify ions"><g class="s1"><g class="mv-pulse"><path d="M52 120q8 -26 8 -30q8 14 8 30z" class="fill" style="fill:#f2c200;opacity:.85"/></g><text x="60" y="145" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">sample in flame</text></g><g class="s2"><line x1="80" y1="95" x2="150" y2="95" class="ln mv-flow"/><path d="M143.7 98L150 95L143.7 92" class="ln"/><path d="M160 70l30 25l-30 25z" class="pt"/><text x="175" y="140" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">spectroscope</text></g><g class="s3"><rect x="220" y="60" width="160" height="40" class="pt"/></g><g class="s4"><rect x="270" y="60" width="4" height="40" style="fill:#f2c200"/><rect x="276" y="60" width="3" height="40" style="fill:#f2c200"/><text x="300" y="120" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">line spectrum</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="300" y="140" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">compare with known spectra</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="162" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Line brightness gives the concentration</text></g></svg>

title: The proportions of different gases in the atmosphere
subject: Chemistry

title: Today's atmosphere
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="About four-fifths nitrogen and one-fifth oxygen"><g class="s1"><path d="M120 85L120 25A60 60 0 1 1 63 104Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.5"/><text x="130" y="100" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">nitrogen ~80%</text></g><g class="s2"><path d="M120 85L63 104A60 60 0 0 1 119 25Z" class="fill hot" style="opacity:.7"/><text x="70" y="60" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">oxygen ~20%</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="290" y="60" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">small amounts of:</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="290" y="85" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">carbon dioxide, water vapour,</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="290" y="105" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">noble gases</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="162" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Much the same for 200 million years</text></g></svg>

title: Earth's early atmosphere
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Volcanoes released carbon dioxide and water vapour that condensed into oceans"><g class="s1"><path d="M40 150L100 70L160 150Z" class="fill" style="opacity:.4"/><text x="100" y="165" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">volcano</text></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:30px;--y:-40px"><circle cx="100" cy="66" r="6" class="fill hot"/><circle cx="110" cy="60" r="5" class="fill hot"/></g><text x="200" y="30" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">CO₂, water vapour, N₂</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="240" y="60" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">little or no oxygen</text></g><g class="s4"><rect x="190" y="130" width="190" height="20" class="fill cool" style="opacity:.4"/><text x="285" y="124" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">water condensed: oceans</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="290" y="90" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">like Mars and Venus</text></g></svg>

title: How oxygen increased
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Algae and plants photosynthesised and oxygen built up"><g class="s1"><path d="M80 140c-10 -30 0 -50 0 -70c0 20 10 40 0 70z" class="fill cool"/><path d="M120 140c-10 -30 0 -50 0 -70c0 20 10 40 0 70z" class="fill cool"/></g><g class="s2"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:0px;--y:-30px"><circle cx="100" cy="120" r="11" class="fill"/><text x="100" y="124" class="cap" text-anchor="middle" style="fill:var(--bg);font-size:7px">CO₂</text></g></g><g class="s3"><g class="mv-slide" style="--x:120px;--y:-20px"><circle cx="100" cy="60" r="10" class="fill hot"/><text x="100" y="64" class="cap" text-anchor="middle" style="fill:var(--bg);font-size:7px">O₂</text></g></g><g class="s4"><text x="280" y="70" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">algae: from 2.7 billion years ago</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="280" y="100" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">oxygen slowly increased</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="162" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen</text></g></svg>

title: How carbon dioxide decreased
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="CO2 was used in photosynthesis and locked in rocks and fossil fuels"><g class="s1"><text x="200" y="24" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">CO₂ in the early atmosphere</text></g><g class="s2"><line x1="200" y1="34" x2="80" y2="80" class="ln mv-flow"/><path d="M84.8 74.9L80 80L87 80.6" class="ln"/><text x="70" y="95" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">photosynthesis</text></g><g class="s3"><line x1="200" y1="34" x2="200" y2="80" class="ln mv-flow"/><path d="M197 73.7L200 80L203 73.7" class="ln"/><text x="200" y="95" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">sedimentary rock</text></g><g class="s4"><line x1="200" y1="34" x2="320" y2="80" class="ln mv-flow"/><path d="M313 80.6L320 80L315.2 74.9" class="ln"/><text x="330" y="95" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">fossil fuels</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="120" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">limestone, coal, crude oil, gas</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="200" y="162" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Some also dissolved in the oceans</text></g></svg>

title: The greenhouse effect
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 170" role="img" aria-label="Short wavelength sunlight passes in; longer wavelength radiation is absorbed"><g class="s1"><circle cx="40" cy="30" r="16" class="fill hot"/><path d="M20 160A200 120 0 0 1 380 160" class="fill cool" style="opacity:.3"/></g><g class="s2"><path d="M0 100Q200 50 400 100" class="pt" style="stroke-dasharray:4 4"/><text x="340" y="85" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">greenhouse gases</text></g><g class="s3"><line x1="60" y1="40" x2="160" y2="135" class="ln mv-flow hot"/><path d="M153.3 132.9L160 135L157.5 128.5" class="ln hot"/></g><g class="s4"><path d="M180 135l10 -10l10 10l10 -10l10 10l10 -10l10 10" class="pt cool"/></g><g class="s5"><line x1="240" y1="130" x2="270" y2="82" class="ln mv-flow"/><path d="M269.2 89L270 82L264.1 85.7" class="ln"/></g><g class="s6"><line x1="270" y1="82" x2="300" y2="125" class="ln mv-flow"/><path d="M293.9 121.6L300 125L298.9 118.1" class="ln"/><text x="320" y="140" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">re-radiated</text></g><g class="s7"><text x="200" y="162" class="cap" text-anchor="middle">Water vapour, CO₂, methane keep Earth warm</text></g></svg>

title: Human activities that increase greenhouse gases

title: GCSE History
summary: The GCSE in twenty-five short chapters: the key words and a few worked lines each for the exam skills — sources, interpretations and the "how far" essay — and the most-taught options: Germany, 1890–1945; Conflict and tension, 1894–1918, 1918–1939 and 1945–1972; Health and the people, c1000 to the present day; Elizabethan England, c1568–1603; Norman England, c1066–c1100; America, 1840–1895; and every other AQA option: Russia, 1894–1945; America, 1920–1973; Conflict in Asia, 1950–1975; the Gulf and Afghanistan, 1990–2009; Power and the people; Migration, empires and the people; Edward I, 1272–1307; Restoration England, 1660–1685; and the historic environment. In the order of the AQA GCSE History (8145) specification; Edexcel's Weimar and Nazi Germany, Superpower relations, Medicine in Britain, Anglo-Saxon and Norman England and the American West cover the same ground.
subject: History

title: √2 is irrational
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 200" role="img" aria-label="Proof by contradiction that the square root of 2 is irrational"><g class="s1"><text x="14" y="26" class="cap" style="font-size:11px;text-anchor:start">1</text><text x="30" y="26" class="cap hot" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">Suppose √2 = a ÷ b, a fraction in</text><text x="194" y="26" class="cap hot" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">lowest terms</text></g><g class="s2"><text x="14" y="56" class="cap" style="font-size:11px;text-anchor:start">2</text><text x="30" y="56" class="cap" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">Square both sides: 2 = a² ÷ b², so a² = 2b²</text></g><g class="s3"><text x="14" y="86" class="cap" style="font-size:11px;text-anchor:start">3</text><text x="30" y="86" class="cap cool" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">a² is 2 × something, so a² is even, and so a is even: a = 2k</text></g><g class="s4"><text x="14" y="116" class="cap" style="font-size:11px;text-anchor:start">4</text><text x="30" y="116" class="cap cool" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">Then 2b² = (2k)² = 4k², so b² = 2k²: b is even too</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="14" y="146" class="cap" style="font-size:11px;text-anchor:start">5</text><text x="30" y="146" class="cap hot" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">Both even: both share the factor 2, not lowest terms. Contradiction.</text></g><g class="s6"><text x="14" y="176" class="cap" style="font-size:11px;text-anchor:start">6</text><text x="30" y="176" class="cap" style="font-size:10.5px;text-anchor:start">So the supposition is false: √2 is irrational ∎</text></g><g class="s5"><line x1="192" y1="22" x2="262" y2="22" class="pt hot" style="stroke-width:2"/></g></svg>

title: A-level Maths: Statistics and Mechanics
summary: The applied half of A-level Maths in fourteen short lessons: sampling, data, probability, the binomial and normal distributions, hypothesis tests and regression, then kinematics, forces, projectiles, friction and moments, each with the key words, formulas, worked lines and two worked examples.
subject: Maths

title: Data presentation and interpretation, with worked examples
topics: Statistics, Histograms, Box Plots & Quartiles, Cumulative Frequency

title: Probability, with worked examples
topics: Probability, Venn Diagrams & Set Notation, Tree Diagrams

title: The binomial distribution, with worked examples
Hypothesis testing with the binomial, with worked examples
The normal distribution, with worked examples
Correlation and regression, with worked examples
Conditional probability, with worked examples
topics: Conditional Probability, Venn Diagrams & Set Notation, Tree Diagrams

title: Kinematics with constant acceleration, with worked examples
Forces and Newton's laws, with worked examples
Friction and inclined planes, with worked examples
A-level Further Maths
summary: The core of A-level Further Maths in eighteen topics, from proof by induction and complex numbers to differential equations, with overviews of further mechanics and further statistics: the ideas, key points, formulas and two worked examples each.
subject: Further Maths

title: De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity
Series and the method of differences
Polar coordinates
topics: Coordinate Geometry (A-Level), Area Under a Curve by Integration

title: Further calculus: volumes, mean values and improper integrals
topics: Integration, Area Under a Curve by Integration

title: Further calculus: integration techniques
topics: Standard Integrals, Integration by Substitution, Integration by Parts

title: A-level Physics
summary: The whole A-level in seventeen sections: the ideas, the key points, the formulas and worked examples for each, following the usual order of a UK A-level Physics specification from measurements to astrophysics.
subject: Physics

title: Astrophysics
topics: Astrophysics, Telescopes, Classification of Stars, Cosmology

title: A-level Chemistry
summary: The whole A-level in nineteen short parts: the ideas, the equations and a worked example or two each, in the usual order of physical, then inorganic, then organic chemistry.
subject: Chemistry

title: A-level Biology
summary: The whole A-level in twenty short parts: the key ideas, the required practicals and a worked example each, in the order of the AQA A-level Biology (7402) specification.
subject: Biology

title: A-level English Literature
summary: The skills and contexts behind every set text: close reading, form and structure, tragedy, comedy and the Gothic, poetry and unseen prose, four critical lenses, context, comparison, coursework and essay planning.
subject: English Literature

title: A-level History
summary: The popular A-level options in overview, from the Tudors, Russia, Germany and the USA to the British Empire, the Cold War and civil rights, with dates, causes, consequences and model essay paragraphs, then the skills: sources, interpretations, essays and the NEA.
subject: History

title: Germany, 1918–1945: Weimar and the Nazi state
The USA, 1865–1945: from Reconstruction to the New Deal
A-level Geography
summary: The whole A-level in sixteen parts: physical systems and hazards, ecosystems, global governance, places, cities, population and resources, then fieldwork and statistics, each with a case study outline, key points and the formulas for the quantitative skills.
subject: Geography

title: The water cycle and drainage basins
Glacial landscapes and cold environments under pressure
Statistical skills: Spearman's rank and chi-squared
A-level Psychology
summary: The whole A-level in seventeen short topics: the key studies, explanations and evaluation points for each, in the order of the AQA A-level Psychology specification.
subject: Psychology

title: The brain, plasticity and biological rhythms
Research methods: data and the scientific process
A-level Sociology
summary: Every perspective and topic of the course: functionalism, Marxism, feminism, interactionism and postmodernism; education and its methods in context; research methods; families; beliefs; crime and deviance; the media; and the science and values debate.
subject: Sociology

title: Families and households: change, diversity and policy
Beliefs in society: religion, change and secularisation
Theory and methods: science, values and social policy
A-level Economics
summary: The whole A-level in eighteen parts: markets, market failure, firms and labour, then the macroeconomy, policy, trade and development, each with a diagram described in words and a worked example, ending with essay technique.
subject: Economics

title: Scarcity, choice and the price mechanism
Market failure: externalities and public goods
Information gaps, intervention and government failure
Economic growth and the business cycle
Monetary policy and the financial sector
Exchange rates and the balance of payments
Essay technique: chains of analysis and evaluation
A-level Business
summary: The whole A-level in sixteen short parts: the key words, the formulas and a few worked lines each, from objectives and leadership through decision tools, the functions and finance to strategy, change and global business.
subject: Business

title: Marketing strategy and the marketing mix
Competitive strategy and methods of growth
A-level Politics
summary: A-level Politics in sixteen short guides: UK democracy, elections, voting systems, voting behaviour, parties and pressure groups; the constitution, Parliament, the Prime Minister and cabinet, the Supreme Court and devolution; liberalism, conservatism, socialism and an optional idea; and comparisons with US government. Each gives examples and a model argument and counter-argument.
subject: Politics

title: A-level Computer Science
summary: The whole A-level in eighteen short topics: programming, data structures and algorithms, the theory of computation, how the machine works, and the project, each with the ideas, a worked example and the points to learn.
subject: Computer Science

title: Linked lists, trees and hash tables
Finite state machines and regular expressions
Ethics, law and the NEA project
A-level Spanish
summary: A-level Spanish in twelve short parts: the advanced grammar that lifts an answer (the subjunctive, conditional sentences, the passive, relative pronouns and reported speech), the themes of the AQA-style course from family to politics, how to write an essay on a film or novel, and the speaking exam with its individual research project.
subject: Spanish

title: The subjunctive in all its uses
Writing an essay on a film or novel
The speaking exam and research project
A-level French
summary: A-level French in twelve short parts: the advanced grammar that lifts an answer (the subjunctive, conditional sentences, the passive, relative pronouns and reported speech), the themes of the AQA-style course from family to politics, how to write an essay on a film or novel, and the speaking exam with its individual research project.
subject: French

title: The subjunctive in all its uses
Writing an essay on a film or novel
The speaking exam and research project
A-level Philosophy and Religious Studies
summary: The foundations A-level Philosophy and Religious Studies share, in eight short chapters: logic, the arguments for God and their critics, the problem of evil, five ethical theories, knowledge, mind, and free will — the key words and a few worked lines each, every side given its strongest case.
subject: Religious Studies

title: Bayes' theorem as areas
html: <svg class="sa" viewBox="0 0 400 200" role="img" aria-label="Bayes' theorem as areas: of everything where B happened, the part where A also holds is P(A given B)"><rect x="40" y="30" width="320" height="130" class="pt"/><rect x="40" y="30" width="80" height="130" class="fill cool"/><text x="80" y="22" class="cap">A: P(A)</text><text x="240" y="22" class="cap">not A</text><g class="s1"><rect x="40" y="70" width="80" height="90" class="fill hot"/><text x="80" y="120" class="cap">P(B|A)P(A)</text></g><g class="s3"><rect x="120" y="140" width="240" height="20" class="fill hot"/><text x="240" y="135" class="cap">P(B|not A)P(not A)</text></g><g class="s5"><text x="200" y="188" class="cap">P(A|B) = left red ÷ all red</text></g></svg>
